data.gender_notes: Charis is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Charis was the goddess of charm, beauty, and the graces. In Christian tradition, Charis represents the divine grace, kindness, and charm bestowed upon us by God. The name Charis carries the meaning “Grace, kindness, charm” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Charis usually hope their child will grow to embody grace, kindness, charm and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes God's endless grace, kindness, and charm towards us

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Charis total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: כריס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם כריס נגזר מהמילה היוונית χαρίς, שפירושה חסד, חן או מתנה. בשורשיו העבריים, המילה קשורה למושג החסד האלוהי והמתנה האלוהית. השם משקף את הרעיון של קבלת מתנה מאלוהים, ומשמש כזכר לחסד ולרחמים של אלוהים.

in_greek.name: Χάρις
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χάρις προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη χαρίς, που σημαίνει χάρη, εύνοια ή δωρεά. Στη Βίβλο, η λέξη χαρίς χρησιμοποιείται για να περιγράψει τη χάρη του Θεού και τη διάθεση του Θεού να δίνει δώρα στους ανθρώπους. Το όνομα Χάρις αντανακλά την ιδέα της λήψης δώρας από τον Θεό και χρησιμεύει ως υπενθύμιση της χάρης και του έλεος του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Charis
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Charis derivatur a verbo Graeco χαρίς, quod significat gratiam, donum, vel beneficium. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Charis referebatur ad gratiam Dei et ad dona quae Deus hominibus concedit. Nomen hoc reflectit ideam acceptationis doni a Deo et servit ut recordatio gratiae et misericordiae Dei.

in_english.name: Charis
in_english.long_meaning: The name Charis originates from the Greek word χαρίς (charis), meaning 'grace,' 'favor,' or 'gift.' In Christian tradition, Charis reflects the concept of receiving a gift from God, symbolizing divine favor and mercy. The name has been used in various Christian cultures to signify the spiritual concept of grace and has been associated with positive personality traits such as kindness, compassion, and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Charis carries a rich cultural background from ancient Greek mythology, where it was the name of a goddess responsible for the feelings of fascination, attraction, delight, and miracle. This goddess's charm and grace extended far beyond personal virtues. She was also the one who helped ensure productive relationships between mortals and deities, and was even present at the birth of the god Apollo. With this heritage, the name Charis emanates a sense of enchantment, attraction, and favor that extends beyond individual personality traits.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Charis holds an enlightening spiritual significance as the representation of God's unending grace, favor, kindness, and charm. It embodies the Christian teaching that God bestows His love, forgiveness, and blessings upon us with an abundant and generous spirit. Charis is a reminder that God's grace extends past our personal actions, and that His love and mercy are ever-present, providing an unending source of comfort, joy, and hope in our lives. The deep spiritual significance of the name Charis inspires gratitude for the divine gift of grace and a daily reminder to share God's love with others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Charis is a Greek word meaning grace or gift from God. It represents the unmerited favor and love bestowed upon us by the Divine. In Christian tradition, it is also the name of the Goddess of Grace and Favor, who is often invoked for her blessings and guidance.

biblical_reference.note: In the New Testament, the concept of χάρις (charis) is central to Christian theology, referring to God's grace and favor.

historical_references.reference: The ancient Greek word χάρις (charis) meant 'grace', 'graciousness', or 'favor'. In the New Testament, it is translated as 'grace', 'graciousness', or 'favor'. The early Christian use of the term was influenced by the Greek concept of agape love, which was understood as a self-giving love, a love that was both unconditional and free.

The name 'Charis' was also given to early Christian martyrs, especially those who were young and died as virgins. The cult of the martyrs developed in the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD, and the veneration of saints was an important aspect of early Christianity. The name 'Charis' was given to these martyrs as a reminder of the divine grace and favor bestowed upon them.
